questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English spoken country outside of Europe. NUS is a highly ranked university in Asia with acknowledged and dedicated professors. Furthermore, I wanted to go to a place with higher temperatures than what we know of in Denmark. And most importantly, Singapore is a great place to travel from - you can easily buy cheap tickets to get to other destinations in Asia, also during the semester.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find the information you needed upon arrival. KU was very helpful to answer whatever questions you may have.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a lot of emails telling us what we needed to do, including making appointments for visa, module registration etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy at all. I expected to get campus housing since I haven't heard of any exchange students who didn't get it offered, but they told us that in the fall 2022 only around 40 % of all exchange students got an on campus housing. Therefore, we were a lot of students looking for accomodation and when you have never been to Singapore it makes it hard for you to know which areas are good etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You should start to look after housing a long time before arrival. 
As I recall, you only find out in mid-July whether you have been granted campus accommodation after various rounds of appeals. Having to find housing in 2 weeks is super stressful, so start to orientate yourself and look for housing well in advance. However, I find an apartment i River Valley which is really a great area, and I enjoyed having an everyday life among locals. You should also know that housing off campus is much more expensive!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a lot of emails telling you what to do and what deadlines you should be aware of. In addition, the staff at NUS also responded quickly to emails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email correspondance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was really happy for only having three classes; 4 credits, 5 credits and 8 credits. Though one of the classes was really intensive, having only three courses made it possible for me to travel a lot during the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They expect you to be prepared for classes, and participate in the discussions. There are many courses where you have to prepare at least one presentation for the class, and your participation in general is also a part of your final grade. However, I didn't have the feeling that the professors where cold calling students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
World Trade Law, 8 credits
International Investment Law, 4 credits 
International Law and Asia, 5 credits

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all my courses. 
WTL is really intensive, and the professor expects a lot from you. The workload is way more than what I have experienced in Copenhagen which is why I never did all the reading. If you just show up for class and familiarize yourself with the judgments, it will be okay but you should be aware that the reading is insane. 
International Investment Law is the best course I have ever had, including the professor. Even though the course was only for three weeks, the professor took time to learn all the students names and it was contagious from how passionated he was about the subject. It was a really interesting course!
International Law and Asia was kind of boring, and you didn't have to show up to classes since the examination is a written assignment where you choose your own topic. Choosing this course makes it possible to travel some more.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I was hoping to get an on campus housing because that would have been much cheaper than having to rent a room. 
Alcohol was also really expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries from supermarkets was really expensive which is why I almost didn't cook dinner. It was, however, possible to buy cheap food at hawker centre.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although those who lived on campus had more opportunities to participate different kinds of sports, there were still some options for the rest of us. I would really recommend starting at something to meet local and other exchange students, especially if you don't get an on campus housing.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sports you can imagine like handball, football, tennis, volleyball, water polo crossfit, board games etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried water polo, tennis and volleyball which was a success.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel! 
You can easily buy cheap flight tickets going to Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Korea etc., and it often does not take long to get to these places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. Singapore is a multicultural country where you can meet all kinds of cultures. Just be open minded and get involved in the different cultures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some different clubs and participate in the events that are arranged.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You have to look for housing in a good time, since you are not guaranteed to get offered on campus housing. 
2. Lower your expectations of your own professionel performance. You just have to pass the courses so don't spend too much time on the reading. 
3. Go travel. Asia is amazing! And as soon as you get out of Singapore everything is much cheaper.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The possibility to travel to other countries during the semester.

questions.answer: Yes
